radEmu differential-abundance analysis

Source: R/rademu.R
step_rademu.Rd

Fit planned contrasts with radEmu::emuFit(). A centralized add_model() defines the fixed design and taxonomic analysis units. The default robust score test is recommended by radEmu; Wald testing is available explicitly.

Usage

step_rademu(
  rec,
  test = c("score", "wald"),
  cluster = NULL,
  max_significance = 0.05,
  p_adj_method = "BH",
  constraint_param = 0.1,
  seed = 130L,
  rarefy = FALSE,
  id = rand_id("rademu"),
  engine_args = list()
)

Arguments

rec

An unprepared Recipe object.

test

Native test to report: "score" (default) or "wald".

cluster

Optional single metadata column identifying dependent observations. NULL uses native independent-observation inference.

max_significance

Adjusted P value cutoff.

p_adj_method

Multiple-testing adjustment passed to p.adjust().

constraint_param

Native pseudo-Huber smoothing parameter, default 0.1.

seed

Integer seed used for native fitting. Restores the caller's RNG.

rarefy

Whether to rarefy before fitting; default FALSE.

id

Unique step identifier.

engine_args

Named list with an optional fit list of native arguments, for example tolerance, maxit, maxit_null, alpha and remove_zero_comparison_pvals. Solver controls can be passed directly in fit. Data, design, clustering, centring functions, fitted-model reuse, tested coordinates, test selection and result shape are managed by dar; control and return_both_score_pvals cannot be overridden.

Value

A Recipe with the radEmu step added.

Details

Effects are natural-log fold differences relative to the native pseudo-Huber centre across analysis taxa. They are not unqualified absolute-abundance changes or log2 fold changes. Each planned contrast is reparameterized and fitted with its own native centring constraint. This retains the native hypothesis rather than treating the nonlinear centre as a linear transformation of previously centred coefficients.

Supply cluster to identify a metadata column containing cluster labels. Labels are aligned with the common model cohort. Clustered inference uses radEmu's GEE framework, not a mixed model. Random-effect formulas such as (1 | subject) are incompatible and are never silently translated. For repeated observations, use a fixed formula and explicitly set cluster = "subject". Missing cluster IDs are not dropped privately.

dar adjusts the selected native P values across returned taxa separately for each planned contrast. It does not adjust across all contrasts jointly. Missing native statistics remain missing, including native zero-comparison exclusions. Native convergence warnings are retained; diagnostics and effective settings are available through get_execution().

The complete taxonomic analysis matrix is used in every fit. Counts are not split by taxon or restricted to the two groups named in a contrast. Score tests can be expensive because each taxon requires a restricted fit. Native numerical validation and errors are left to radEmu.

See also

Other Diff taxa steps: step_aldex2(), step_aldex3(), step_ancom(), step_corncob(), step_deseq(), step_lefse(), step_linda(), step_maaslin(), step_wilcox()

Examples

data(metaHIV_phy)
rec <- recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  add_model(~ RiskGroup2, targets = "RiskGroup2", tax_level = "Genus") |>
  step_rademu()
# prep(rec) executes native score tests for every planned contrast and taxon.
